:::{#def-adam}
#### Adam

Let $f$, $\vx^{(0)}$, $\steplen$ and $\epsilon$ be as in an [adaptive method](#def-adaptive-method),
and let $\beta_1, \beta_2 \in [0, 1)$.
Write $\vg^{(t)}$ for $\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t-1)})$.
The **Adam** method [@kingma2015adam] is defined, for $t = 1, 2, \ldots$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vm^{(t)} &\eqdef \beta_1\,\vm^{(t-1)} + (1 - \beta_1)\,\vg^{(t)} \\
u_j^{(t)} &\eqdef \beta_2\,u_j^{(t-1)} + (1 - \beta_2)\,\paren{g_j^{(t)}}^2 \\
\est{\vm}^{(t)} &\eqdef \frac{\vm^{(t)}}{1 - \beta_1^t} \\
\est{u}_j^{(t)} &\eqdef \frac{u_j^{(t)}}{1 - \beta_2^t} \\
x_j^{(t)} &\eqdef x_j^{(t-1)} - \steplen\,\frac{\est{m}_j^{(t)}}{\sqrt{\est{u}_j^{(t)}} + \epsilon},
\end{aligned}
$$

for each coordinate $j = 1, \ldots, p$, with $\vm^{(0)} \eqdef \vzero$ and $u_j^{(0)} \eqdef 0$.

:::
